original_value: This paper presents a novel and practical convolutional neural network architecture to implement semantic segmentation for side scan sonar (SSS) image. As a widely used sensor for marine survey, SSS provides higher-resolution images of the seafloor and underwater target. However, for a large number of background pixels in SSS image, the imbalance classification remains an issue. What is more, the SSS images contain undesirable speckle noise and intensity inhomogeneity. We define and detail a network and training strategy that tackle these three important issues for SSS images segmentation. Our proposed method performs image-to-image prediction by leveraging fully convolutional neural networks and deeply-supervised nets. The architecture consists of an encoder network to capture context, a corresponding decoder network to restore full input-size resolution feature maps from low-resolution ones for pixel-wise classification and a single stream deep neural network with multiple side-outputs to optimize edge segmentation. We performed prediction time of our network on our dataset, implemented on a NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier, and compared it to other similar semantic segmentation networks. The experimental results show that the presented method for SSS image segmentation brings obvious advantages, and is applicable for real-time processing tasks.

result.paraphrase: This paper introduces a novel, practical convolutional neural network architecture for semantic segmentation of side scan sonar (SSS) images. As a commonly used marine survey sensor, SSS produces higher-resolution views of the seafloor and underwater targets. Yet SSS imagery poses several challenges: severe background-pixel imbalance, speckle noise, and intensity inhomogeneity. We describe a network and training strategy designed to address these three key issues in SSS image segmentation. The proposed approach uses fully convolutional neural networks and deeply supervised nets to perform image-to-image prediction. Its architecture includes an encoder that captures context, a matching decoder that reconstructs full-resolution feature maps from low-resolution ones for pixel-wise classification, and a single-stream deep neural network with multiple side outputs to improve edge segmentation. We evaluated the network’s prediction time on our dataset using an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier and compared it with other similar semantic segmentation networks. Experimental results indicate that the proposed SSS image segmentation method offers clear advantages and is suitable for real-time processing tasks.
